html:
The Menominee are an Algonquian people of northeastern Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Their name comes from the Ojibwe word for "wild rice people", after the wild rice they gathered from the lakes; they call themselves Mamaceqtaw, "the people".

Their oral history places their origin at the mouth of the Menominee River, and they are among the oldest peoples of the region. Their neighbours were the Ho-Chunk and Potawatomi. From the 1600s they traded furs with New France. In the 1800s they ceded most of their land but refused removal west and kept a forest reservation, which they log carefully to this day. The United States ended its recognition of the tribe in 1961; the Menominee won it back in 1973.
